- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment or price; cap forecast at +10% above recent peak if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model often lags; forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of true price.
- Mean reversion bias: if model is consistently above true price for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out extremes with 3-day moving average filter.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with true trend; match sentiment direction with 2-day lag.
